routes.name: Visa-free short stay
routes.summary: Citizens of visa-free countries can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 days across the Schengen area, Greenland and the Faroe Islands. Check the official list for your passport.

other: Passport valid 3 months past departure and issued in the last 10 years
Enough money for the trip, roughly DKK 350 per day or DKK 500 per day in a hotel
Not on any entry ban or sanctions list

Citizens of Australia, Canada, Chile, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea and the US have separate stay rules (90 days or 3 months) that can be affected by earlier Nordic stays

stay.note: Same limit applies to Schengen, Greenland and the Faroe Islands combined.

sources.label: List of visa-free and visa-required countries

routes.name: Short-stay visa for private and tourist visits
routes.summary: Schengen visa for people from visa-required countries. Stay up to 90 days in any 180 days. Apply at a Danish mission or visa center, or online.

other: Passport valid 3 months past visa expiry, issued in the last 10 years, 2 blank pages
Travel insurance covering all Schengen countries, at least EUR 30,000
Enough funds, roughly DKK 350 per day or DKK 500 per day in a hotel
Some nationalities need a host in Denmark, who fills out an invitation (VU2 form recommended)

steps: Host in Denmark completes the invitation if needed
Apply in person at the Danish mission or visa center, or online at ApplyVisa.um.dk
Pay the fee and give fingerprints

routes.name: Short-stay visa for business visits
routes.summary: Schengen visa for business trips to a Danish company. Up to 90 days in any 180 days. You cannot do paid work.

other: Host company must be registered in the Danish CVR and the business relationship must already exist
Travel insurance with at least EUR 30,000 cover and enough funds
Paid trainees normally need a work permit instead

routes.name: Pay Limit Scheme
routes.summary: Work and residence permit for any job paying at least DKK 552,000 a year (2026). No specific education or field needed.

other: At least 30 hours a week
Pay and terms must meet Danish standards
Salary paid into a Danish bank account in your name, opened within 180 days
Amount is adjusted each 1 January

stay.note: Normally 4 years if the job lasts that long, otherwise the length of the job plus an automatic 6-month job-seeking permit with no work rights.

routes.processing: Normally 1 month, up to 3 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Supplementary Pay Limit Scheme
routes.summary: Work permit for any job paying at least DKK 446,000 a year (2026). No specific education needed.

other: Amount is adjusted each 1 January

stay.note: Normally 5 years if the job lasts that long, otherwise the length of the job.

routes.processing: Normally 2 months, up to 5 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Positive List for People with a Higher Education
routes.summary: Work permit for jobs on the Positive List when you have a matching higher education. Titles can come off the list, so check the current list.

eligibility.education: Higher education matching the job title (bachelor's, professional bachelor's or master's)
other: Job title must be on the Positive List
Usually full time, about 37 hours a week, with a Denmark-registered employer
Pay must not be below normal for the field. No fixed amount is set.
Some jobs need Danish authorization

stay.note: Length of the job if under 4 years, otherwise normally 4 years. A 6-month job-seeking permit may follow, with no work rights.

routes.processing: Normally 1 month, up to 3 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Positive List for Skilled Work
routes.summary: Work permit for skilled jobs on the Positive List (updated each 1 January and 1 July). The employer must meet apprentice training targets.

other: Job must be on the list (DISCO-08 codes)
Employer registered in Denmark and meeting its Laereplads-AUB apprentice targets
Pay and terms must meet Danish standards
Salary paid into a Danish bank account in your name, opened within 180 days

stay.note: Length of the job if under 4 years, otherwise normally 4 years. Tied to one job and company.

routes.processing: Normally 3 months, up to 4 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Fast-Track Scheme
routes.summary: Faster work permits through employers certified by SIRI. Tracks: pay limit, supplementary pay limit, short-term, researcher and educational.

other: Employer must be SIRI-certified
Pay limit track needs DKK 552,000 a year, supplementary pay limit track DKK 446,000 a year (2026)
Short-term track allows up to 90 days in any 365 days, applied for stay by stay

stay.note: Pay limit and educational tracks up to 4 years. Supplementary track up to 5 years.

routes.processing: Standard about 1 month. Quick job start normally about 10 days. Supplementary track 2 months, up to 4.

routes.name: Start-up Denmark
routes.summary: Residence and work permit to run an innovative start-up. Your idea must first be approved by an expert panel. Up to 75 people a year, up to 3 per team.

other: Business idea approved by the Danish Business Authority expert panel before applying
Must own part of the business and run it actively
Self-support (2025 levels): DKK 153,240 alone, DKK 306,480 with spouse, DKK 356,904 with spouse and children, DKK 203,664 with children only
Restaurants, retail and small trades generally do not qualify

stay.note: First permit up to 2 years, extensions up to 3 years at a time.

routes.processing: Normally 2 months, up to 4 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Residence permit for higher education
routes.summary: Study permit for full-time state-approved or accredited higher education. Part-time study does not qualify.

savings.note: For stays over one year, 12 months of funds, up to DKK 89,112 (2026).

other: Admitted to a full-time programme at an accredited or state-approved institution
Language skills to follow the course

stay.note: Work up to 90 hours a month September to May and full time June to August on state-approved programmes.

routes.processing: Normally 2 months, up to 3 months if more information is needed.

routes.name: Working Holiday
routes.summary: One-year working holiday permit for young people from partner countries. Salaried work only, not permanent, no family along.

savings.note: Plus a return ticket. Varies by country, up to DKK 24,000 for New Zealand.

other: Age limits: Australia and Canada under 36, South Korea under 35, New Zealand under 31
Work up to 6 months within the year (9 for South Korea)
The page also lists Argentina, Chile and Japan as partners. Their rules were not confirmed here, so check the official pages.

routes.name: EU/EEA, Swiss and Nordic citizens: right to reside
routes.summary: EU/EEA, Swiss and Nordic citizens can live and work in Denmark without a work permit. Stays over 3 months need an EU residence document, which has no fee. UK citizens cannot use this route.

other: Workers, students and people with enough funds qualify
Self-supporting: funds at least equal to the cash benefit rate, DKK 7,095 a month for a single person (2026), documented for 12 months
Job seekers can stay up to 6 months without a document
Stays under 3 months need no application

sources.label: Residence as EU/EEA, Swiss or Nordic citizen

routes.name: Permanent residence under EU rules
routes.summary: After 5 consecutive years of real residence under EU rules, EU/EEA/Nordic citizens and their non-EU family members can get permanent residence.

other: 5 years of actual residence, not just a registered address
Short absences under 6 months a year are fine
Non-EU family members must apply themselves, no earlier than one month before 5 years

stay.note: Right is kept until you leave Denmark for 2 years or more.

routes.name: Family reunification: spouse or partner
routes.summary: Residence permit to join a spouse or partner in Denmark who is a Danish citizen, permanent resident or refugee. Strict conditions on age, housing, language and a financial guarantee.

other: Both partners normally 24 or older
Valid marriage, or 18 months of living together
Couple must meet 4 of 6 integration conditions, including a mandatory one for the partner in Denmark
Partner in Denmark needs own suitable home, self-support and a financial guarantee of DKK 61,709.34 (2026)
Pass Danish A1 within 6 months and A2 within 9 months of the permit
Other family members such as children and parents have separate rules not covered here

routes.name: Permanent residence permit
routes.summary: Normally 8 years of legal residence. It can be 4 years if you meet all four extra requirements, and you need Danish and steady work.

eligibility.language: Prøve i Dansk 2 (Prøve i Dansk 3 counts as an extra requirement)
other: Over 18 and still meet your current permit conditions
Full-time work or self-employment for 3 years 6 months of the past 4 years
Currently working at least 15 hours a week
No overdue public debt, no certain benefits in the past 4 years, no disqualifying criminal record

Need 2 of 4 extra requirements for the 8-year route, all 4 for the 4-year route: Dansk 3, 4 years full-time work, active citizen exam, average taxable income of DKK 346,155.57 a year over 2 years (2026)
Exemptions exist, for example for pensioners and people with disabilities

fees.label: Fee for family reunification or asylum

routes.name: Danish citizenship by naturalization
routes.summary: Normally 9 years of residence, Danish language test, a citizenship test and steady work. Parliament passes a naturalization bill twice a year. Shorter periods apply to some groups.

eligibility.language: Danish test 3 (Dansk 3), or Dansk 2 if you have not received certain social assistance
other: 9 years of continuous residence normally. 8 for refugees and stateless people, 2 for Nordic citizens, 6 to 8 for spouses of Danish citizens
Permanent residence for at least 2 years (1 for refugees and stateless people)
Pass the 2021 naturalization test
Full-time work or self-employment for 3 years 6 months of the past 4 years
Self-sufficient, no certain overdue debts, no disqualifying criminal record
Dual citizenship was not confirmed on the pages read. Applicants resident in Greenland must give up their previous citizenship.

citizenship.note: Bills go to Parliament in April and October. Greenland and the Faroe Islands are separate for some rules.

routes.processing: About 14 months on average for 2021 cases, then Parliament takes 2 to 3 months.

routes.name: Danish citizenship by descent
routes.summary: A child born on or after 1 July 2014 automatically gets Danish citizenship if the father, mother or co-mother is Danish. Older births follow the rules in force at the time.

other: Children born abroad who become Danish before 22 fall under special retention rules. Details were not confirmed here.
Rules for children born outside marriage between 11 October 1993 and 30 June 2014 are on the official page

citizenship.note: Only the parent generation was confirmed. Dual citizenship rules not confirmed.
